header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Liu (Redwood SE), Ava Thompson (Spark UX CTO), Diego Morales (Lead ML Eng), Samir Patel (PM)
summary: Intro discovery to align on fast path to first call (TTFT), evaluate free credits vs reserved/private pilot, and surface security requirements. Customer leaning PLG/self-serve to start but wants benchmarks and an architecture check for PII/PHI. Agreed next steps: send credits & security pack, bench spreadsheet, schedule a short bench run next week.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit
Security: SOC2 / SAML / KMS / audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood. Cool, we can do quick intros.
[00:09] Ava Thompson: Hi, Ava here — CTO at Spark UX. We're looking to prototype a conversational assist in our design tool, want to see what TTFT looks like and what cost profile is.
[00:17] Connor Liu: Hi Ava, Connor, solutions engineer. I usually run the bench tests and help set up quickstarts.
[00:22] Diego Morales: Diego — I own infra/ML at Spark. We're sensitive about data residency and want to understand private options versus just spinning up hosted API tokens.
[00:31] Samir Patel: Samir, PM, driving the timeline. We want something in-prod-ish in 6–8 weeks if it looks good.
[00:36] Maya Patel: Awesome. Agenda: quick overview of Redwood quickstart & credits, discuss TTFT plan and sample bench, and then walk hosting options — hosted, dedicated, private (VPC/on-prem). Save time at the end for security questions. Sound good?
[00:46] Ava Thompson: Yep. Also curious about whether we can start on hosted with credits and then move to private with minimal changes.
[00:53] Connor Liu: Totally. That's one of the typical PLG-to-enterprise paths. The API surface stays the same, and we have migration patterns. The biggest lift is network setup and KMS for private.
[01:03] [speaker overlap] Diego Morales: When you say "private" you mean V P C with a customer control plane?
[01:07] Connor Liu: Yes, our Private deployment can either run in your VPC or on-prem; you'll manage the VPC peering / VPC endpoints and we support KMS/HSM integrations. For quickstarts you can use hosted and we provide isolated tokens.
[01:18] Maya Patel: On credits — we'll provide starter credits that map to token usage; we can pre-load an account so you can run a TTFT bench without billing friction.
[01:26] Ava Thompson: Nice. How fast is TTFT in practice — like from repo to first request in engineering terms?
[01:33] Connor Liu: For a self-serve path it's typically < 4 hours for a simple text generation call if you have an engineer. That's from sign-up to first successful call. For embedding/workflow plus SDK integration it's more likely same-day. For a bench run we prepare a small prompt set and a benchmarking script — usually we can guide your infra engineer through it in 30–60 minutes.
[01:48] Diego Morales: What about throughput and latency numbers? We target median p95 latency < 200ms for short prompts, and want to estimate token cost.
[01:57] Connor Liu: We publish model profiles in our catalog; depending on the model family you pick, the hosted API average could be 60–300ms for short context sizes on our verified models. For predictability, Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and more consistent p95, and Private lets you tune hardware and quantization.
[02:12] Samir Patel: If we start hosted with credits and then want to reserve capacity, how disruptive is that?
[02:18] Maya Patel: Not disruptive at all — you can pin model versions and rollout policies. It's mostly a config change and a billing/contract shift for Dedicated; code calls stay identical.
[02:27] Ava Thompson: Good. Security: we need SOC2 and SSO. Does Redwood have SOC2 and SAML?
[02:34] Connor Liu: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II. SSO/SAML is supported for enterprise accounts and we emit audit logs. For Private deployments you can point to your KMS for key control.
[02:44] Diego Morales: And data retention? We may need short retention or no retention for certain endpoints.
[02:49] Connor Liu: We have retention controls and can set no-retain for enterprise customers or Private installs. For hosted we have options to opt out of long-term retention; we'll provide the security pack with exact controls.
[02:59] [03:00] Maya Patel: I'm going to drop the links in the chat: quickstart guide, security pack, and a benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:05] [link paste] Maya Patel: Quickstart: https://redwood.ai/quickstarts/spark-ux 
[03:09] Maya Patel: Security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/spark-ux-brief 
[03:12] Connor Liu: Benchmark sheet (sample prompts + metrics): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/spark-ux-bench.xlsx
[03:18] Ava Thompson: Perfect. Can you give a sample TTFT plan? Step-by-step?
[03:23] Connor Liu: Sure. Step 1: we give you credits and a sandbox key. Step 2: run our bench script that hits 10–20 prompts at varying sequence lengths (we provide them). Step 3: we look at latency/cost and suggest model/quantization knob — often switching to a quantized variant reduces cost 2–3x with small latency increase. Step 4: if you like results, spin a reserved Dedicated pool or request a Private eval.
[03:45] Diego Morales: That quantization — is it automatic or do we need model changes?
[03:50] Connor Liu: It depends on the model; for many open models we provide quantized variants you can call directly. For private deployments there's an extra build step but the runtime supports it. There can be some small quality regressions; Redwood Optimize recommends settings per workload.
[04:04] Samir Patel: Pricing question: the credits convert to token usage right? Are there separate charges for streaming or function-calling?
[04:11] Maya Patel: Credits map to per-token usage and embedding units and we break out streaming overhead separately in the bill; I'll send a pricing example in the SOW.
[04:20] Ava Thompson: We're also evaluating Bedrock and Anthropic — what's the differentiator for Redwood at this stage?
[04:27] Maya Patel: Two main points — production-first tooling across hosted/dedicated/private with the same API, and optimizations that reduce per-token cost (auto-batching, KV caching, prefix caching). Also, clear observability by route and token-level cost breakdown so you can measure unit economics easily.
[04:44] Diego Morales: Observability is big for us. Do you expose tracing hooks or integrate with our existing APM?
[04:50] Connor Liu: Yes, we have tracing hooks and integrations (OpenTelemetry, Datadog). You can sample traces and map them to tokens/requests in the console.
[04:58] Ava Thompson: About data residency — we have EU customers, some data must stay in EU. How flexible is regional hosting?
[05:05] Connor Liu: Hosted API supports region routing and we can pin workloads to regions. Private deployment also supports your on-prem or EU cloud region. We'll note this in the security pack.
[05:14] Samir Patel: Timeline again: we want a minimal viable integration in 6–8 weeks but ideally have TTFT and bench run next week.
[05:21] Maya Patel: Great — propose we allocate ~2–4 hours next week for the bench. Connor: can you run that with Diego?
[05:27] Connor Liu: Yup. Diego, what's your availability?
[05:30] Diego Morales: I can do Tues/Wed afternoon PST next week.
[05:33] Connor Liu: I'll propose Wed 3pm PT and send calendar invite.
[05:36] [06:00] Ava Thompson: Quick technical — if we go private on-prem, what are the minimal hardware requirements?
[06:06] Connor Liu: For small pilots you can run on a single DGX or equivalent, but for production we recommend a multi-GPU pool. We'll share a hardware guidance doc. Quantized models allow lower memory footprint so you can use T4/RTX-class hardware for some families.
[06:20] Diego Morales: Any special networking like eBPF or kernel tuning?
[06:24] Connor Liu: Not generally, standard VPC peering and endpoint is fine; we have recommendations for high-throughput setups. We'll include a checklist.
[06:33] Samir Patel: Who are the internal champions we should expect on Redwood side during pilot?
[06:37] Maya Patel: I'll be your AE for commercial side, Connor will run the bench and pilot setup. If it moves to Dedicated/Private we'll loop in an Engineering Account Manager and Solutions Architects.
[06:49] Ava Thompson: Awesome. Any gotchas you usually see with customers starting from PLG?
[06:54] Connor Liu: A couple: not setting prompt sets for consistent evals, not accounting for prefix/KV cache effects when comparing to locally hosted models, and underestimating token billing for system messages or long histories.
[07:07] Diego Morales: About KV cache — we've seen K V cash referenced in other docs, can you explain how that affects latency?
[07:12] Connor Liu: Sure — KV cache stores previous key/value states for autoregressive generation, so after warm-up repeated contexts are much faster. For chat where context grows, cache management matters. That K V cache greatly reduces recomputation and improves p95 for follow-up tokens.
[07:30] [08:00] Maya Patel: I want to call out that we provide a canary/fallback model policy so if a model variant is saturated we can route to cheaper fallback automatically. That helps with reliability in PLG bursts.
[08:10] Ava Thompson: That matters. We do expect bursts from usage in our design editor.
[08:14] Connor Liu: We'll also show batch sizing and throughput graphs — it's in the bench sheet.
[08:19] [09:00] Diego Morales: For security assessment, do you have an SOC2 report we can share with our security team?
[09:05] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll include SOC2 and an ISO summary in the security pack. Also SAML configuration guide and audit log retention options.
[09:15] Samir Patel: Any limit on free credits? We need enough to run a representative bench and integrate basic SDKs.
[09:21] Maya Patel: We'll provision starter credits that should cover a 2–4 hour bench and some SDK integration testing. If you need more we can top up depending on scope.
[09:30] Ava Thompson: Great. Let's talk success criteria — what would Redwood define as success for this pilot?
[09:36] Connor Liu: Success typically: (1) TTFT bench completes with p95 < target (your 200ms goal or a negotiated figure), (2) cost per 1k tokens within target, (3) integration of SDK in your app and a canary route to Redwood, (4) security sign-off for hosted path or a private install plan.
[09:57] Ava Thompson: For us also low friction to escalate to Dedicated if we see production traffic.
[10:02] Maya Patel: Makes sense. We'll aim to make that path clear in the SOW.
[10:07] [15:00] Connor Liu: Quick note — sometimes model names and acronyms get garbled in transcripts, so when you review the benchmark sheet the model slug may look like rdx-3b-q8_ or similar.
[15:12] Diego Morales: That's fine.
[15:15] Maya Patel: I'll recap next steps: send credits and quickstart link today, security pack and SOC2 within 24 hours, Connor shares bench sheet and proposes Wed 3pm PT for the bench. Diego to confirm. Any other questions?
[15:30] Ava Thompson: One more on routing policies — can we prefer EU region for EU users and US for US users?
[15:35] Connor Liu: Yes, we can set routing by policy based on geo or tenant. We'll include a sample config.
[15:41] Samir Patel: Also log retention for debugging — can we get 30 days of high-res traces?
[15:45] Connor Liu: Yes; we have tiered storage for traces and token logs. We'll call that out in pricing.
[15:51] Maya Patel: Great. If nothing else, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and calendar invites.
[15:59] Ava Thompson: Thanks, excited to try this out.
[16:02] Diego Morales: Thanks all.
[16:04] Samir Patel: Thanks.
[16:10] [End of recording]

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors (model slugs, acronyms). References included to quickstart guide, security pack, benchmark sheet. Action items captured above.
